entries.title: The Beginning
entries.body: Cameron and Sophie stepped aboard Juno's 7 in Kos to begin their first season working together on the same yacht. A grainy marina webcam captured the start of the story.
entries.summary: The moment Cameron and Sophie stepped aboard together and the season became their shared story.

crewMoment.title: First day aboard
crewMoment.body: A grainy marina webcam preserved something no polished photograph could recreate: the unrepeatable moment the two of them arrived to begin their first season on the same yacht.

didYouKnow.title: Kos and the sea routes of the Dodecanese
didYouKnow.body: Kos sits beside sea lanes that have linked the Greek islands with Asia Minor for centuries. The modern marina is part of a much older pattern of people arriving, departing and moving between islands.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Kos
flavourOf.body: Kos is known for relaxed island cooking: grilled fish, tomato-rich stews, honey, soft cheeses and mezze shared beside the water.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Greek island table with grilled fish, mezze, cheese, honey and bread

entries.title: Lipsi Voyage Stop
entries.body: Juno's 7 spent time at Lipsi during the yacht's early run through the Dodecanese, adding another quieter Greek island stop before continuing on to Patmos.
entries.summary: A quiet Dodecanese stop between the early Greek island passages.

didYouKnow.title: Lipsi's quiet place in the Dodecanese
didYouKnow.body: Lipsi lies between Patmos and Leros. Its sheltered harbour and slower pace make it a favourite with sailors looking for quieter island stops.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Lipsi
flavourOf.body: Harbour tables tend towards grilled octopus, fresh fish, local cheeses and small plates made for long, unhurried meals.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Greek island table with grilled fish, mezze, cheese, honey and bread

entries.title: Settling In
entries.body: Cameron settled into the rhythm of deck work: preparing lines, handling fenders, washdowns and the careful details behind every smooth arrival.
entries.summary: Cameron settling into the day-to-day rhythm of deck work aboard Juno's 7.

crewMoment.title: Settling into deck work
crewMoment.body: Cameron was getting used to the practical routine on deck: preparing lines, handling fenders, washdowns and the dozens of small tasks that make a yacht appear effortless from the quay.

didYouKnow.title: A polished yacht never stays finished
didYouKnow.body: Salt, sun and spray begin undoing a washdown almost as soon as it is complete. Exterior maintenance is a continuous rhythm rather than a job that is ever truly finished.

entries.title: First Days on Deck
entries.quote: Giving the sun deck black some love. / Spent the last 3 days cleaning the thing and tbh, still filthy.
entries.body: The early days aboard quickly became a cycle of cleaning, polishing and keeping the yacht looking immaculate beneath the Mediterranean sun. Cameron summed it up with a perfectly honest follow-up after three days of work: the yacht was still filthy.
entries.summary: Cameron captures the early rhythm of deck work in Patmos: polishing, cleaning and still seeing the next job immediately.

crewMoment.title: Salt never sleeps
crewMoment.body: The photographs show the contrast at the heart of the season: beautiful anchorages surrounding practical, physical work. However immaculate the yacht looks from shore, salt, sun and dust keep giving the crew another job to do.

entries.title: Rather Rocky
entries.quote: Rather rocky.
entries.body: The sea showed a livelier side during the late morning passage.
entries.summary: A short video that preserves the movement and mood of the sea better than a still photograph could.

didYouKnow.title: Aegean moods
didYouKnow.body: A short passage between islands can change character quickly. Calm water can become lively within the same watch, making even a few seconds of video an important part of the story.

entries.title: Sophie's First Jet Ski
entries.quote: Captain was going out on the Ski with his Mrs who’s onboard as well and he asked me if I wanted to take Soph out so we went out on one for 15 minutes.
entries.body: The captain invited Cameron to take Sophie out on a jet ski. It became Sophie's first time on one.
entries.summary: Fifteen minutes on the water became one of Sophie's first memorable moments of the season.

crewMoment.title: A first together
crewMoment.body: The captain invited Cameron to take Sophie out while he used the other jet ski. It was Sophie's first time on one and a rare little pocket of shared fun inside a working day.

didYouKnow.title: Water toys are also deck work
didYouKnow.body: Launching, recovering, cleaning and securing jet skis and inflatable toys is part of everyday guest operations for the deck team.

entries.title: Katapola Harbour
entries.body: Juno's 7 stopped at Katapola Harbour on Amorgos as the yacht continued west through the Cyclades. The harbour formed a practical link between the early Greek island stops and the later move towards Ios.
entries.summary: A practical Amorgos harbour stop during the early Greek island passage.

entries.title: Ios Harbour
entries.body: Juno's 7 spent time in Ios Harbour before the later anchorage at Agios Ioannis Bay. The stop helps complete the Ios sequence, linking the yacht's harbour visit with the quieter anchorage where Sophie's next-house photo was taken.
entries.summary: A harbour stop on Ios before the later anchorage at Agios Ioannis Bay.

entries.title: My Future House
entries.quote: My future house!
entries.body: Passing a beautiful hillside house above the water, Sophie captured one of those light-hearted travel moments that instantly becomes part of the shared story.
entries.summary: One passing hillside villa and a message that instantly became part of the family story.

didYouKnow.title: Cycladic Gem
didYouKnow.body: The hillside villa Sophie jokingly picked out as her future house appears to be Cycladic Gem, a private villa above Agios Ioannis Bay that is available to rent for events: https://cycladicgem.com/

entries.title: A Short Video from Sophie
entries.body: A moving postcard from the season: a small video memory that belongs alongside the route and photographs.
entries.summary: A moving postcard: water, wind and atmosphere that would be difficult to describe later.

didYouKnow.title: Why the small clips matter
didYouKnow.body: Video keeps the sound and movement around a moment. Years later, those few seconds may restore the atmosphere more vividly than a carefully composed photograph.

entries.title: Nice Spot for Today
entries.quote: Nice spot for today.
entries.body: A quiet anchorage surrounded by clear water and green hills. The toys were out, the tender was alongside, and the day had the stillness that makes the Greek islands unforgettable.
entries.summary: Clear water, green hills and the quiet satisfaction of a good anchorage.

crewMoment.title: A simple message home
crewMoment.body: Cameron's four words did not need embellishment. The photographs and video show exactly why the place earned them.

didYouKnow.title: Zakynthos from the water
didYouKnow.body: The island is best known for dramatic limestone coasts and intensely blue coves. From a yacht, the quieter sheltered bays can be every bit as memorable as the famous viewpoints.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Zakynthos
flavourOf.body: Island cooking brings together olive oil, local cheeses, grilled meat and fish, sweet pastries and long meals close to the sea.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Greek island table with grilled fish, mezze, cheese, honey and bread

entries.title: Sami Harbour
entries.body: Juno's 7 stopped at Sami Harbour on Kefalonia as the yacht crossed the Ionian islands. It marked a useful staging point between Zakynthos and the move north towards Paxos and Corfu.
entries.summary: A Kefalonia harbour stop during the Ionian passage north.

entries.title: Underway — Changing Conditions
entries.quote: Underway for another 2.5 hours. / A little stormy today. / Cam on a mission.
entries.body:
The day began with a calmer underway view from Cameron: open sea ahead, teak decks in the sun and around two and a half hours still to run. Later, Sophie sent a different side of the same passage: a little stormier, more unsettled, and a reminder of how quickly conditions can change at sea.

Sophie also captured Cameron towing the yacht's inflatable water toys from the tender. It was one of those practical deck-crew moments that sits behind the guest experience: getting equipment safely into position and managing it in livelier conditions. It has since been confirmed that no-one was on the toys at the time.
entries.summary: The same day told from two sides: calm teak and open water, then livelier conditions and deck work.

crewMoment.title: Cam on a mission
crewMoment.body: Sophie captured Cameron towing the yacht's inflatable toys from the tender. No-one was riding them; this was the practical work of moving equipment safely in changing conditions.

didYouKnow.title: Passage days are still working days
didYouKnow.body: Being underway does not pause the deck routine. Equipment must stay secure, weather is watched continuously and jobs change with the sea state.

entries.title: Gaios Harbour Anchorage
entries.body: Juno's 7 anchored at Gaios Harbour Anchorage on Paxos before continuing north towards Corfu. The stop sits within the sheltered harbour approach and forms part of the yacht's Ionian passage towards the Adriatic.
entries.summary: A sheltered Paxos anchorage before the move north to Corfu.

entries.title: Barbati Anchorage
entries.body: Juno's 7 anchored off Barbati on Corfu's east coast, adding a quieter coastal stop before the yacht moved further south towards Garitsa Bay.
entries.summary: A quieter anchorage on Corfu's east coast before Garitsa Bay.

entries.title: Garitsa Bay
entries.body: Later the same day, Juno's 7 moved to Garitsa Bay near Corfu Town. This anchorage became the final Greek stop before the long passage north towards Cavtat and Croatia.
entries.summary: The final Greek anchorage before the passage north towards Croatia.

entries.title: Underway to Cavtat
entries.quote: Off to Cavtat, 2 hours in to our 18 hour trip there.
entries.body: Juno's 7 is making one of the longest passages of the season, heading north-west from Corfu towards Cavtat on Croatia's southern coast. Two hours into the eighteen-hour crossing, the Adriatic stretches away beneath clear skies while the yacht leaves a broad white wake behind her. Faithfully following in that wake is SETE, the chase boat, keeping station astern as both vessels make their way towards Croatia together.
entries.summary: Eighteen hours across the Adriatic, with SETE holding station astern in the wake.

crewMoment.title: Two hours into eighteen
crewMoment.body: Cameron sent the update early in one of the longest passages of the season. The broad white wake and the chase boat behind turn the simple message into a real sense of distance.

didYouKnow.title: Crossing into a new chapter
didYouKnow.body: The passage from Corfu to Cavtat carried Juno’s 7 from the Greek islands into the Croatian Adriatic, changing both the landscape and the character of the voyage.

entries.title: Very Pretty Here
entries.quote: Very pretty here! / Yeah just been able to come off for lunch with two of the other deck crew.
entries.body:
After the long passage north-west from Corfu, Juno's 7 has arrived in Cavtat, the first Croatian chapter of the season. The contrast with the overnight crossing could hardly be stronger: clear Adriatic water against the stone waterfront, shaded trees along the promenade, terracotta roofs, and mountains rising behind the bay.

Sophie summed up the first impression perfectly: "Very pretty here!"

For the crew, arrival also brought the chance to step ashore. Cameron was able to get off the yacht for lunch with two of the other deck crew, a small but welcome pause after the rhythm of a long sea passage. These are the moments that make the journal feel real: not just the places Juno's 7 visits, but the brief windows of time when the crew can enjoy them too.

With Juno's 7 lying off the waterfront and Cavtat opening around them, the voyage has moved from the Greek islands into a new stretch of the Adriatic story.
entries.summary: Sophie’s first impression of Cavtat, followed by Cameron’s welcome chance to get ashore for lunch.

crewMoment.title: Lunch with the deck crew
crewMoment.body: After the long passage, Cameron was able to step ashore with two of the other deck crew. That small window away from the yacht is part of the destination story too.

didYouKnow.title: Cavtat before Cavtat
didYouKnow.body: The modern town stands close to the site of ancient Epidaurum. Its sheltered bay has welcomed travellers and sailors for far longer than the stone waterfront suggests.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Cavtat
flavourOf.body: The southern Dalmatian table centres on grilled Adriatic fish, black risotto, olive oil, figs, citrus and crisp local white wine.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Dalmatian seafood table with grilled fish, octopus salad, black risotto, figs and wine

entries.title: She’s a Biggie!
entries.quote: She’s a biggie!
entries.body: While Juno's 7 was in the sheltered waters around Polače, Black Pearl appeared nearby. Her three masts and unmistakable silhouette made this the first true notable encounter of the journal.
entries.summary: A quiet Mljet anchorage shared with one of the most recognisable sailing yachts in the world.

notableEncounter.title: Black Pearl
notableEncounter.body: Black Pearl is a 106.7 metre three-masted sailing yacht. Her unmistakable DynaRig silhouette is among the most distinctive in the world. Charter guide: from approximately €850,000 per week, plus expenses.

didYouKnow.title: A Roman palace beside the anchorage
didYouKnow.body: Polače takes its name from the substantial late-Roman palace remains beside the harbour. Juno’s 7 was anchored within sight of history built into the modern village.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Mljet
flavourOf.body: Seafood, olive oil, herbs and local white wine suit the island’s quiet, forested setting.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Dalmatian seafood table with grilled fish, octopus salad, black risotto, figs and wine

entries.title: Lumbarda Anchorage
entries.body: Juno's 7 anchored off Lumbarda on Korčula after the Mljet stop, using the quieter water east of Korčula Town before moving into port later that day.
entries.summary: A quiet anchorage east of Korčula Town before moving into port.

entries.title: Korčula Port
entries.body: Juno's 7 later moved into Korčula Port, bringing the yacht alongside one of Croatia's best-known island towns after the nearby Lumbarda anchorage.
entries.summary: A port stop at Korčula after anchoring nearby at Lumbarda.

entries.title: Coming Into Anchorage
entries.location: Velo Ždrilo Anchorage, Pakleni Islands, Croatia
entries.quote: Coming in to anchorage today.
entries.body:
After Korčula, Juno’s 7 approached the Pakleni Islands and settled into the sheltered water around Palmižana. The route shifted from open passage back to the close detail of an island anchorage.

A separate photograph from the day shows Cameron driving the small tender carried inside Juno's 7's internal garage.
entries.summary: An approach through the Pakleni Islands and a peaceful anchorage off Hvar.

didYouKnow.title: The name is not really about hell
didYouKnow.body: Pakleni is often translated as “hellish”, but the name is linked to paklina, the pine resin once used for waterproofing wooden boats.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Hvar
flavourOf.body: Hvar brings grilled fish, octopus salad, olive oil, herbs and local wines into an island setting known for both glamour and quiet coves.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Dalmatian seafood table with grilled fish, octopus salad, black risotto, figs and wine

entries.mapStop: Velo Ždrilo Anchorage, Pakleni Islands, Croatia

entries.title: Peaceful Night Shift
entries.quote: Peaceful night shift.
entries.body: The photograph and message arrived in the early hours while Juno’s 7 was underway. Later that day the yacht continued towards Split and moored near the Riva waterfront.
entries.summary: A quiet watch at sea before the next busy harbour chapter.

crewMoment.title: The view from watch
crewMoment.body: The glamorous destinations sit around watches, handovers and long working days. A peaceful night shift is still a night at work, but occasionally the sea gives something back.

didYouKnow.title: Split grew inside a Roman palace
didYouKnow.body: Diocletian’s Palace was built around the beginning of the fourth century. Rather than remaining an isolated ruin, its streets and buildings became part of the living city.

entries.title: A Familiar Family Resemblance
entries.body: Moored in Split, Juno’s 7 found herself beside Triumph. The connection made the encounter especially personal: Triumph is a sister ship of Calex, the yacht on which Cameron completed his first season.
entries.summary: A notable neighbour connected directly to Cameron’s own yachting story.

notableEncounter.title: Triumph
notableEncounter.body: The encounter mattered less because of fame and more because of familiarity. Triumph’s connection to Calex quietly linked Cameron’s first yacht season with the season now unfolding aboard Juno’s 7.

crewMoment.title: Two seasons connected
crewMoment.body: The owner of Juno’s 7 has known the owner of Calex for many years, adding another small thread between the yachts and Cameron’s route into the industry.

entries.title: Together Ashore
entries.body: A photograph shared on 10 July captured Cameron and Sophie together on a quay, with yachts moored behind them. The exact marina is not confirmed, so the picture is kept as a simple record of the two of them ashore rather than tied to an uncertain location or occasion.
entries.summary: A straightforward photograph of Cameron and Sophie together ashore, preserved without guessing at the marina or occasion.

crewMoment.title: Together, away from the working day
crewMoment.body: The photograph matters because it records the two of them together. No extra story is needed where the details are not known.

entries.title: Dolphins off Milna
entries.body:
While Juno’s 7 lay at anchor near Milna, dolphins appeared beside the yacht. Cameron’s own footage caught a lovely breach, while the captain’s drone supplied the best view from above.

The accompanying photographs hold the calm setting around the encounter: blue water, quiet decks and the Croatian coast beyond.
entries.summary: Dolphins beside the yacht, then the captain’s drone lifting the view above the anchorage.

crewMoment.title: A lovely breach
crewMoment.body: Cameron’s phone footage captured the close-up moment; the captain’s drone then turned it into a wider memory of dolphins moving through the anchorage.

entries.title: Getting the Dents Out
entries.quote: Getting dents out the teak (Because some idiot dropped a fender hook onto it — they weigh about 5kg 'ish).
entries.body: A damp towel, a hot iron and a little patience became the repair kit after a heavy fender hook landed on the teak. The steam encourages the compressed wood fibres to rise again — a small, careful job that says a great deal about the standards expected on deck.
entries.summary: A five-kilogram fender hook, a dented teak deck and a practical lesson in putting things right.

crewMoment.title: The less glamorous side of yacht life
crewMoment.body: The spectacular locations come with painstaking maintenance. Even a small dent in the teak becomes a job to solve properly.

entries.title: A Film Set — and Ash on the Deck
entries.quote: Mamma Mia 2 was filmed in the place we are docked right now.
entries.body:
Vis brought one of those family-chat discoveries that instantly changes how a place feels. Sophie’s message prompted Ellis to reply: “you’re joking me and dad need to go”.

Later, the day gained a more sobering detail. Fine ash from the wildfire on Korčula was drifting across the Adriatic and landing on Juno’s 7, connecting the calm sunset above Vis with events unfolding on another island.
entries.summary: A famous film location, a family reaction and ash arriving across the Adriatic from Korčula.

didYouKnow.title: Vis on screen
didYouKnow.body: Much of Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again was filmed on Vis, with the island standing in for the fictional Greek setting of Kalokairi.

crewMoment.title: Ellis had an immediate plan
crewMoment.body: The family-chat response was instant: “you’re joking me and dad need to go”.

entries.title: Afternoon Off
entries.body: During his afternoon off, Cameron shared a photograph of his and Sophie’s feet splashing in the clear water. It was a simple pause together after a busy stretch aboard.
entries.summary: No itinerary and no grand event — just a few hours together beside the Adriatic.

crewMoment.title: Capture moments, not just movements
crewMoment.body: The route map records where the yacht went. This quiet photograph records how an afternoon off felt, which may matter even more when the season is remembered years later.

entries.title: Much Nicer
entries.quote: Much nicer hahahaa.
entries.body:
Cameron’s 6am video showed steady rain and a noticeably choppy sea near the start of his shift. A little later, the view had transformed: blue skies over Vis harbour, the church on the left, the harbour entrance ahead and teak decks in the foreground.

The day delivered another surprise too: “I finish at 14:00 today!?! Unreal”. For someone accustomed to early starts and much longer days, an afternoon finish was a genuine bonus.
entries.summary: A wet and choppy 6am start gave way to blue skies — and an unexpectedly early finish.

crewMoment.title: Finished by 14:00
crewMoment.body: “I finish at 14:00 today!?! Unreal” was a rare bonus after the long days that normally define the working rhythm aboard.

entries.title: Ready for the Climb
entries.body: Helmet on, radio checked and harness secured: Cameron was photographed in full working-at-height gear in Vis harbour. It is one of the clearest glimpses yet of the practical skill and safety discipline behind everyday deck work.
entries.summary: A proper day-at-work portrait, with Vis harbour and two thousand years of history behind it.

crewMoment.title: Not every office has a view like this
crewMoment.body: The setting is spectacular, but the equipment tells the real story: helmet, lifejacket, radio, harness and working lines all in place before the task begins.

didYouKnow.title: A Roman theatre beneath the monastery
didYouKnow.body: Across the harbour, the Church and Franciscan Monastery of St Jerome on the Prirovo Peninsula stand over the remains of a Roman theatre dating to around the first century AD.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Vis
flavourOf.body: Vis is known for seafood, slow-cooked island dishes, local wine and the kind of harbour meals that feel rooted in the landscape.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Dalmatian seafood table with grilled fish, octopus salad, black risotto, figs and wine

entries.title: Another Dolphin
entries.location: Underway off Biševo, later anchored off Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia
entries.quote: Another dolphin — on the bow underway.
entries.body:
Juno’s 7 left Vis and took a looping route south-west towards Biševo before turning back to anchor off Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia. During the passage, another dolphin appeared beneath the bow.

Cameron captured it moving alongside the yacht, while Sophie’s second video preserved something just as memorable: the delighted shriek of one of the owner’s children as the dolphin came into view.
entries.summary: A roundabout passage towards Biševo, another dolphin at the bow and an excited voice that says everything.

crewMoment.title: The sound of the moment
crewMoment.body: The dolphin is the sight everyone watched, but the spontaneous shriek of excitement is what makes Sophie’s video feel alive.

didYouKnow.title: Back into Mamma Mia country
didYouKnow.body: Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia was one of the Vis locations used in Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again — an especially fitting place to end the day’s looping passage.

entries.title: Dawn over Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia
entries.location: At anchor off Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia, Vis
entries.body: Before the harbour had properly woken, Cameron looked east across Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia as the first light of day rose behind the hills of Vis. With Juno’s 7 lying quietly at anchor and the water almost mirror-calm, it was one of those peaceful Mediterranean mornings that few visitors experience from this viewpoint.
entries.summary: First light over Mamma Mia town, seen from the stillness of the anchorage.

didYouKnow.title: Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia became Kalokairi
didYouKnow.body: Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia was one of the principal Vis locations used as the fictional Greek island of Kalokairi in Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again.

entries.title: Potkućina Bay
entries.body: Juno's 7 anchored in Potkućina Bay on Kakan as the yacht continued through the islands of central Dalmatia. The stop adds another sheltered anchorage to the route before the move further north through the Kornati area.
entries.summary: A sheltered Kakan anchorage during the move north through central Dalmatia.

entries.title: Calm Before the Storm
entries.quote: A storm is just about to hit us 🥴
entries.body:
As evening settled over Smokvica Vela, the underwater lights beneath Juno’s 7 transformed the sea around the tender into a glowing turquoise pool. Beyond it, the anchorage faded into the deep blue of the Adriatic.

The apparent calm was deceptive. Sophie’s next update explained that the storm looked large on the radar and the crew were moving the yacht to find better shelter. The later AIS track showed only a short repositioning within the same anchorage rather than a move to another bay.
entries.summary: A luminous, almost perfectly calm anchorage — moments before the crew repositioned for an approaching storm.

crewMoment.title: Radar told a different story
crewMoment.body: “Moving the boat now to find a bit of shelter apparently the storm is looking big on the radar!” The sea looked calm, but the captain was already acting on what the weather radar showed.

entries.title: North through Kornati
entries.body: After the overnight weather watch at Smokvica Vela, Juno’s 7 headed north-west through the Kornati islands and anchored in Lapatica Bay on the south-west side of Kornat Island, opposite Piškera.
entries.summary: A purposeful morning departure and another quiet anchorage deeper in the Kornati archipelago.

entries.title: Levrnaka Bay
entries.location: Levrnaka Bay, Kornati National Park, Croatia
entries.body: Juno’s 7 spent the night in the sheltered waters off Levrnaka as the yacht continued north through Croatia’s Kornati islands.
entries.summary: A quiet night in the sheltered waters of Levrnaka Bay.
entries.mapStop: Levrnaka Bay, Kornati National Park, Croatia

entries.title: First Light at Levrnaka
entries.location: Levrnaka Bay, Kornati National Park, Croatia
entries.quote: Good night
entries.body: In the early hours, Cameron shared a peaceful dawn view across the anchorage with the simple message “Good night” — meaning that the night at anchor had gone well, rather than that he was heading to bed. The calm water and first light over the surrounding hills captured a beautifully uneventful overnight watch.
entries.summary: A tranquil dawn after a good night at anchor off Levrnaka.

crewMoment.title: A good night, not goodnight
crewMoment.body: Cameron’s brief message meant that the overnight anchorage had gone well — exactly the kind of quiet night the crew hopes for.

entries.mapStop: Levrnaka Bay, Kornati National Park, Croatia

entries.title: Hiljača Anchorage
entries.location: Hiljača Anchorage, Žut, Croatia, sheltered by Gušćak Islet
entries.quote: Scampi-1 Soph-0
entries.body: After moving to the sheltered waters of Hiljača Anchorage, Žut, Croatia, protected by the small island of Gušćak, Cameron and Sophie went ashore for dinner at Konoba Vison. Sophie ordered scampi expecting the familiar breaded version served at home, but received whole Adriatic langoustines in tomato sauce instead. One escaped while she was cracking it open, sending sauce across her white trousers and putting Cameron firmly in the splash zone. The evening ended with an encounter with Strawberry, a free-roaming local donkey.
entries.summary: An authentic seafood dinner, a flying langoustine and an unexpected meeting with Strawberry the donkey.

crewMoment.title: Scampi – 1, Soph – 0
crewMoment.body: “Slipped right out my hands when I was cracking it open. Cam was in the splash zone.”

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Žut
flavourOf.body: Croatian škampi are Adriatic langoustines, commonly served whole in a buzara-style sauce of tomato, garlic, olive oil, white wine and herbs — very different from breaded British scampi.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Žut scampi served whole at dinner

entries.title: Superyacht Company in Zadar
entries.body: While moored in Zadar, Juno’s 7 shared the harbour with the striking 52-metre motor-sailer Reposado. Built in Croatia by Tramontana Yachts and delivered in 2024, her twin-masted profile made her stand out even among the harbour’s impressive line-up.
entries.summary: Juno’s 7 shared Zadar Harbour with the distinctive Croatian-built Reposado.

notableEncounter.title: Reposado
notableEncounter.body: Reposado is a 52-metre Tramontana motor-sailer delivered in 2024, accommodating up to 12 guests with a crew of 10. Charter guide: €115,000–€155,000 per week, plus expenses.

entries.title: An Evening at Antiquus
entries.body: After a busy day aboard, Cameron and Sophie headed ashore together for dinner at Antiquus Sushi & More in Zadar. The colourful sushi boat made the evening feel like a proper break from yacht life and added another memorable meal to their Croatian season.
entries.summary: A well-earned evening ashore together over sushi in Zadar.

crewMoment.title: Time ashore together
crewMoment.body: A relaxed meal gave Cameron and Sophie a chance to step away from the working day and enjoy Zadar together.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Zadar
flavourOf.body: Zadar’s restaurant scene reaches well beyond traditional Dalmatian cooking, with modern Asian menus and seafood-led dishes sitting naturally alongside the city’s Adriatic flavours.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Colourful sushi boat from Antiquus Sushi and More in Zadar

entries.title: An Accident on the Dock
entries.body: While cleaning Juno’s 7’s windows from the dock in Zadar, deckhand Toni was concentrating on the glass above him and did not realise he had reached a flight of concrete steps. He fell down the steps and partly into the water, fracturing his radius near the elbow joint. His arm was placed in a full cast, with a repeat X-ray planned after a week and an initial recovery estimate of three to four weeks.
entries.summary: A serious dockside fall left Toni with a fractured radius and his arm immobilised in a full cast.

entries.title: Likely Blue Cave Excursion
entries.body:
One recovered video shows Cameron and the crew on a planned cave excursion aboard a small local excursion boat rather than SETE. The setting appears to be the Blue Cave on Biševo, and the route from Vis towards Komiža Anchorage, Vis Island, Croatia includes a clear loop down towards Biševo on 13 July.

Because the exact date and cave have not been directly confirmed by Cameron and Sophie, the clip remains preserved as an undated season highlight rather than being forced into the main chronology.
entries.summary: A recovered cave-excursion clip, likely from the Blue Cave on Biševo, preserved cautiously as an undated season highlight.

crewMoment.title: Likely location, not confirmed date

entries.title: Beach Club CCTV Moments
entries.body: Two recovered onboard CCTV clips capture the less polished side of deck work around the yacht’s beach club area. One clip shows a deckhand ending up in the water, while an earlier clip shows the same deckhand being knocked and breaking his Meta glasses. They are kept as Crew Life moments rather than dated voyage stops because their exact dates have not yet been confirmed.

crewMoment.body: The clips are labelled by their source as onboard CCTV, not by the person who later shared them.

entries.title: A Quiet View in Kablin Bay
entries.body: While anchored in Kablin Bay, Sophie shared the view aft from Juno’s 7 across clear turquoise water towards the wooded shoreline of Zverinac Island. With an inflatable kayak floating alongside and the bay almost perfectly still, it captured the calm of another sheltered Croatian anchorage.
entries.summary: A peaceful aft-deck view across the sheltered water of Kablin Bay.

entries.title: Snorkelling Mishap at Michelle
entries.location: Michelle Shipwreck, near Sakarun Bay, Dugi Otok, Croatia
entries.quote: Went to a snorkelling point with all the guests, got headbutted by another snorkeller and the glass mask I had on smashed everywhere haha - luckily just a small cut and swelling there
entries.body: Before the later beach setup, Cameron accompanied the owner’s guests by SETE to the Michelle shipwreck, one of the best-known snorkelling spots near Dugi Otok. The trip produced an unexpected collision: another snorkeller headbutted him, shattering the glass mask he was wearing. Fortunately, the result was limited to a small cut and swelling, leaving him with a story rather than anything more serious.
entries.summary: A guest snorkelling excursion to the Michelle shipwreck ended with a smashed mask and a small cut.

didYouKnow.title: The Michelle wreck
didYouKnow.body: The Michelle shipwreck rests in shallow, clear water near the northern coast of Dugi Otok, making it a popular snorkelling destination for boats visiting Sakarun Bay.

entries.title: Waiting on Sakarun Beach
entries.quote: Set the beach up for the guests, now waiting here haha
entries.body: Later that day, Cameron sent a photo from Sakarun Beach after helping set up for the owner’s guests. With the yellow parasols ready, a cold Corona and crisps on the table, and the bay stretching out beyond the beach, it captured a well-earned pause while he waited for the guests to arrive.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes beach setup moment at Sakarun, complete with a brief pause before the guests arrived.

crewMoment.title: Behind the guest experience
crewMoment.body: The photo shows the quiet waiting time after the setup work is done but before the guests arrive.

entries.title: Zadar Anchorage
entries.body: Juno’s 7 returned to the anchorage off Zadar after several days around Dugi Otok so that one of the owner’s guests, who had been staying aboard for a few days, could be transferred ashore. While the yacht remained at anchor, SETE made the run into Zadar before returning to the vessel.
entries.summary: A practical return to Zadar Anchorage for an owner’s guest departure while SETE handled the transfer ashore.

entries.title: Arrival in Crotone
entries.body: After the long passage south from Zadar and across to Italy, Juno’s 7 arrived in Crotone Old Harbour in time for breakfast. It marked the yacht’s first confirmed Italian stop of the season and brought the voyage from the Croatian islands into Calabria on the Ionian coast.
entries.summary: Juno’s 7 reached Crotone Old Harbour after the long passage from Croatia, marking the first confirmed Italian stop of the season.

didYouKnow.title: In the heart of Magna Graecia
didYouKnow.body: Crotone began as the ancient Greek colony of Kroton in the eighth century BC. The city is closely associated with Pythagoras, who founded his school there, and nearby Capo Colonna preserves remains of the sanctuary of Hera Lacinia.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Calabria
flavourOf.body: Calabrian food is known for bold, sun-warmed flavours: chilli, oregano, wild fennel, aubergines, cured pork, cheeses such as pecorino and caciocavallo, and a glass of Cirò from the region’s prized vineyards.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Calabrian table with red chillies, cheeses, cured pork, aubergines and red wine

entries.title: Arrival in Malta
entries.body:
After leaving Crotone in the early hours of 28 July, Juno’s 7 completed the passage south across the Ionian Sea and came into Malta in time for breakfast. The yacht settled at Grand Harbour Marina on the Vittoriosa side of the water, with Valletta and the fortified Three Cities wrapped around one of the Mediterranean’s great natural harbours.

The owners had flown ahead to Malta after leaving the yacht in Zadar, so the arrival also brought Juno’s 7 back into position to meet them again after the delivery passage.

Later that afternoon, Sophie shared a view across Grand Harbour Marina. Lasata was still visible nearby, while Xarifa 1927 had already moved on.
entries.summary: Juno’s 7 reached Grand Harbour Marina in Vittoriosa after the passage from Crotone, completing the crossing from Italy to Malta.

didYouKnow.title: Fort St Angelo and Grand Harbour
didYouKnow.body: Fort St Angelo stands at the end of the Birgu peninsula, immediately beside the marina, and has dominated Grand Harbour for centuries. The Order of St John made it their headquarters after 1530, it played a major role during the Great Siege of 1565, and it later served as a Royal Navy shore base.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Malta
flavourOf.body: Maltese food blends Mediterranean island cooking with strong Sicilian and North African influences: flaky pastizzi, ftira bread with tuna, olives and capers, slow-cooked rabbit stew, lampuki pie, local cheeses, honey and date-filled imqaret.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Maltese table with pastizzi, ftira, rabbit stew, lampuki pie, olives, imqaret and harbour water beyond

notableEncounter.title: Superyacht company in Valletta
notableEncounter.body: Grand Harbour immediately put Juno’s 7 among some serious company. Aquila, the 85.6-metre Derecktor motor yacht, is publicly listed for charter from about €945,000 per week, plus expenses. The classic 49.9-metre schooner Xarifa 1927 was another standout, with current broker listings describing her as not available for charter. Stardust, a 62.5-metre Amels 206 delivered in 2020, and Lasata, a 65.7-metre Rossinavi delivered in 2023, were also visible nearby; for Lasata, public charter listings point to enquiry or POA pricing rather than a published weekly rate.

entries.title: Comino Anchorage
entries.body: With the owners back on board and four guests joining them for a few days, Juno’s 7 left Grand Harbour and anchored off Comino. While the yacht remained at anchor, SETE took the guests across to the Blue Lagoon for an excursion. Later, Sophie shared the evening view across the anchorage, with Comino’s limestone cliffs and cave openings catching the last warm light.
entries.summary: Juno’s 7 anchored off Comino while SETE took the owners and their guests to the Blue Lagoon for an excursion.

didYouKnow.title: Blue Lagoon and Crystal Lagoon
didYouKnow.body: Comino sits between Malta and Gozo and is famous for clear turquoise water. The Blue Lagoon is the best-known swimming spot, while nearby Crystal Lagoon is more enclosed, with cliffs, caves and deeper blue water. Together they make Comino one of Malta’s most recognisable cruising areas.

entries.title: Dwejra Bay
entries.body:
Juno's 7 moved across from Comino to the west coast of Gozo and anchored in Dwejra Bay. After the busy waters around Comino, the stop brought the yacht into one of Gozo's most dramatic coastal settings, surrounded by limestone cliffs, deep blue water and the open Mediterranean beyond.

It was a quiet entry in the journal, but a useful one: the bay marks the first confirmed Gozo stop of the season and adds another Maltese island to the route.
entries.summary: Juno's 7 anchored in Dwejra Bay on Gozo, adding a quiet but striking Maltese stop after Comino.

didYouKnow.title: Dwejra and the lost Azure Window
didYouKnow.body: Dwejra is one of Gozo's best-known coastal areas. It includes Dwejra Bay, Fungus Rock, the Inland Sea and the Blue Hole dive site. The area was also home to the Azure Window, the natural limestone arch that collapsed during a storm in March 2017.

entries.title: Ashore in Syracuse
entries.quote: Just ordered some food
entries.body:
After Juno's 7 reached Porto Grande in Syracuse, Cameron managed to get ashore for food in Sicily while Sophie was still working. His first update was simple: "Just ordered some food."

The meal turned into a proper Sicilian welcome: shrimp ravioli as a starter, followed by calamari for the main course.
entries.summary: Cameron got ashore for food in Syracuse after Juno's 7 reached Porto Grande, while Sophie was still working.

didYouKnow.title: Ortigia and ancient Syracuse
didYouKnow.body: Syracuse was one of the most important Greek cities in the ancient Mediterranean. Its historic centre, Ortigia, sits beside Porto Grande, where Juno's 7 moored after the passage from Malta. The city is also famously linked with Archimedes, whose inventions became part of the legend of Syracuse during its Roman siege.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Sicily
flavourOf.body: Sicilian food reflects the island's position in the middle of the Mediterranean, with Greek, Arab, Spanish and Italian influences layered together over centuries. Around Syracuse, seafood is an obvious highlight, from pasta and shellfish to fried calamari, citrus, tomatoes, capers and local olive oil.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Shrimp ravioli served during Cameron's meal ashore in Syracuse
flavourOf.imageCaption: Journal photo from Cameron's meal ashore in Syracuse

entries.title: Stopped for a Drink
entries.quote: Stopped for a drink
entries.body:
The day after Juno's 7 reached Syracuse, Cameron shared a quiet moment ashore from a cafe table by the waterfront. His message was simply: "Stopped for a drink."

With the sea beyond the railings and Ortigia close by, it captured a small pause during the yacht's first stop in Sicily. He also mentioned finding green apple ice cream from an ice cream place during his walk.
entries.summary: Cameron stopped for a drink ashore in Syracuse and found green apple ice cream during a walk through the city.

entries.title: Dinner and Drinks in Syracuse
entries.quote: It was good - I went back for a nap as I was knackered and then went back out with Soph for dinner and drinks just now x
entries.body:
After a stop ashore earlier in the day, Cameron headed back for a nap before going out again with Sophie for dinner and drinks in Syracuse.

He later messaged: "It was good - I went back for a nap as I was knackered and then went back out with Soph for dinner and drinks just now x."

The restaurant had been recommended by the owners after they had eaten there the previous evening, and they treated the crew to dinner there too. Cameron summed it up simply: "Yeah it was lovely."
entries.summary: Cameron and Sophie enjoyed dinner and drinks ashore in Syracuse after the owners recommended the restaurant to the crew.

entries.title: Anchor Drag at Capo Passero
entries.quote:
Sailing yacht just bumped into our yacht hahahaha
Bit of damage to the paint on the hull.
entries.body:
While Juno's 7 was anchored at Capo Passero, Cameron sent an unexpected update: "Sailing yacht just bumped into our yacht hahahaha." A follow-up explained there was "a bit of damage to the paint on the hull."

In a later voice message, Cameron described how he and Tom had just left with the guests on the smaller Williams tender when they saw a small sailing yacht only a few metres off Juno's 7's bow. The other yacht appeared to have dragged its anchor after the wind picked up, with its anchor becoming caught on Juno's 7's anchor chain.

With guests and children aboard the tender, Cameron and Tom could not safely put themselves between the two vessels. Instead, they used the tender to push the sailing yacht away before Cameron jumped aboard to help separate it from Juno's 7. The result was a scrape and some paint damage rather than the far more serious impact that could have happened if the sailing yacht had continued drifting towards Juno's 7's bow.
entries.summary: A small sailing yacht dragged its anchor at Capo Passero and bumped Juno's 7, leaving paint damage but avoiding a much more serious collision.

entries.title: Choppy Morning to Syracuse
entries.quote: Very choppy morning!!
entries.body:
During the passage from Capo Passero Anchorage towards Syracuse, Sophie sent two short videos from the water with the simple update: "Very choppy morning!!"

It was a useful reminder that even a relatively short leg around Sicily could feel lively once the wind and sea state picked up.
entries.summary: Sophie shared two videos from a choppy morning passage between Capo Passero Anchorage and Syracuse.

entries.title: Dolphins on the Passage to Sicily
entries.body: Cam captured a short TikTok from the Malta to Sicily passage, with dolphins breaking the surface beside the boat over bright blue water. It fits neatly with the long underway leg from Gozo toward Sicily and gives the passage a more vivid moving-memory version than a still photo could.
entries.summary: A dolphin-filled TikTok from the Malta to Sicily passage.

entries.title: Return to Syracuse Anchorage
entries.location: Porto Grande Anchorage, Syracuse, Sicily, Italy
entries.mapStop: Porto Grande Anchorage, Syracuse, Sicily, Italy
entries.body: After the stop at Capo Passero, Juno's 7 returned north to Syracuse and anchored in Porto Grande. It was a practical pause in one of Sicily's great natural harbours before the yacht continued on towards Riposto and Mount Etna.
entries.summary: Juno's 7 returned to Syracuse and anchored in Porto Grande before continuing north along Sicily's east coast.

entries.title: Mount Etna from Porto dell'Etna
entries.location: Porto dell'Etna Marina, Riposto, Sicily, Italy
entries.mapStop: Porto dell'Etna Marina, Riposto, Sicily, Italy
entries.body: While Juno's 7 made her way towards Porto dell'Etna Marina and later settled alongside in Riposto, Cameron and Sophie shared a sequence of views of Mount Etna: first from the water before reaching the harbour, then from the marina as evening fell, and finally after dark as the volcano glowed above the town. The marina's name felt especially appropriate: from the waterfront, the dome and illuminated bell tower of Riposto's Basilica di San Pietro stood out below the volcano, while a red volcanic glow was visible high on Etna's slopes during an active eruptive phase.
entries.summary: Cameron and Sophie shared views of Mount Etna before and after Juno's 7 reached Porto dell'Etna Marina, ending with the volcano glowing above Riposto after dark.

didYouKnow.title: Riposto beneath Europe's most active volcano
didYouKnow.body: Riposto's Basilica di San Pietro is dedicated to St Peter, patron saint of the town and of sailors, making it a fitting landmark beside Porto dell'Etna Marina. Behind it rises Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano and one of the world's most closely monitored. INGV bulletins for 9 August reported active vents and lava flows high on the volcano, and longer-term satellite studies have found lava being emitted for roughly a quarter of the 1970-2010 period.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Etna
flavourOf.body: Etna gives eastern Sicily a food identity of its own: pistachios from Bronte, citrus from the volcanic slopes, honey, almonds and wines grown in mineral-rich soil around the volcano.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Etna-region table with pistachios, citrus, honey, bread and wine

entries.title: Taormina Anchorage
entries.body:
After leaving Porto dell'Etna Marina at Riposto, Juno's 7 made the short passage north along Sicily's east coast and arrived at Taormina Anchorage during the morning.

The stop placed the yacht below one of Sicily's most famous coastal towns, with Taormina sitting high above the Ionian Sea and the coastline around Capo Taormina nearby. The cape is also known for its rocky shoreline, small sea caves and grottoes, giving the anchorage a natural point of interest as well as the view back towards the town.
entries.summary: Juno's 7 made the short passage from Riposto to Taormina Anchorage, close to Capo Taormina's rocky shoreline and sea caves.

didYouKnow.title: Taormina above the Ionian Sea
didYouKnow.body: Taormina is famous for its ancient theatre, first built by the Greeks and later adapted by the Romans. Its position high above the Ionian Sea gives one of Sicily's classic views, with Mount Etna often visible beyond the stage and coastline.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of Taormina
flavourOf.body: Around Taormina, Sicilian cooking leans into citrus, seafood, caponata, swordfish, granita and almond sweets. It is close enough to Etna for volcanic-soil wines and pistachio desserts to feel part of the same table.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Taormina-style Sicilian table with swordfish, caponata, citrus, granita and almond sweets

entries.title: Basiluzzo Anchorage
entries.quote: we are right next to 'V' Toto Wolffs yacht
entries.body:
After the longer run north from Taormina, Juno's 7 anchored off Panarea at Basiluzzo Anchorage in the Aeolian Islands.

The afternoon also brought a notable neighbour. Cameron spotted V nearby and messaged: "we are right next to 'V' Toto Wolffs yacht".
entries.summary: Juno's 7 anchored at Basiluzzo Anchorage off Panarea, where Cameron spotted V nearby.

notableEncounter.title: V
notableEncounter.body: While anchored at Basiluzzo Anchorage, Juno's 7 was lying close to V, the yacht associated with Formula One team principal Toto Wolff. Cameron spotted the neighbour and sent the update: "we are right next to 'V' Toto Wolffs yacht".

didYouKnow.title: Panarea and the Aeolian Islands
didYouKnow.body: Basiluzzo sits among Panarea's smaller satellite islets in the Aeolian Islands, a volcanic archipelago recognised by UNESCO for the way its islands illustrate ongoing volcanic processes. The setting feels remote, but it is part of one of the Mediterranean's most distinctive island chains.

entries.title: Stromboli Volcano Watch
entries.location: Off Stromboli, Aeolian Islands, Sicily, Italy
entries.quote: Soph may get better videos as I'm off to bed but we're near Stromboli now and it's popping off
entries.mapStop: Off Stromboli, Aeolian Islands, Sicily, Italy
entries.body:
Later in the evening, as Juno's 7 made a slow cruise-by off Stromboli in the Aeolian Islands, Cameron sent a short video of the volcano active in the distance. His message captured the moment simply: "Soph may get better videos as I'm off to bed but we're near Stromboli now and it's popping off."

The VesselFinder waypoints show Juno's 7 moving in closer to Stromboli at low speed before continuing towards Lipari, making this a passage moment rather than an anchorage.
entries.summary: Cameron sent a short video while Juno's 7 was off Stromboli, with the volcano active in the distance.

didYouKnow.title: Stromboli and the lighthouse of the Mediterranean
didYouKnow.body: Stromboli is one of the world's most persistently active volcanoes. Its regular bursts of activity have long been visible from the sea, earning it the nickname the lighthouse of the Mediterranean, and the word Strombolian is used for this style of volcanic eruption.

entries.title: Lipari Anchorage
entries.location: Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage, Lipari, Sicily, Italy
entries.mapStop: Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage, Lipari, Sicily, Italy
entries.summary: Juno's 7 continued through the Aeolian Islands and arrived at Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage after the night-time cruise-by off Stromboli.
entries.body:
After the slow cruise-by off Stromboli, Juno's 7 continued on towards Lipari and arrived at Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage in the early hours. It marked another Aeolian stop after a night shaped by volcanic islands rather than harbour towns.

Nearby Vulcano offered a quieter contrast: despite the name, its volcanic alert level was Green at the time, a small anti-climax after the recent glow from Etna and Stromboli.

didYouKnow.title: Lipari, obsidian and pumice
didYouKnow.body: Lipari is the largest of the Aeolian Islands and has been important since prehistoric times. Its obsidian was once traded widely across the Mediterranean, while the island later became known for pumice quarried from its pale volcanic slopes.

flavourOf.title: Flavour of the Aeolian Islands
flavourOf.body: The Aeolian table is strongly shaped by the sea and volcanic islands: capers, olives, tomatoes, fresh fish, pasta, herbs and sweet Malvasia wine all suit a chain of islands where meals often feel tied to the water.
flavourOf.imageAlt: Aeolian Islands table with capers, olives, tomatoes, fish, pasta, bread and Malvasia wine

entries.title: Sunglasses Watch
entries.location: Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage, Lipari, Sicily, Italy
entries.quote: Cam ensuring that a third pair of sunglasses was not lost 🫠
entries.mapStop: Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage, Lipari, Sicily, Italy
entries.body:
During the evening at Faraglioni di Lipari Anchorage, Sophie sent a short video of Cameron taking no chances with another pair of sunglasses. Her message summed it up neatly: "Cam ensuring that a third pair of sunglasses was not lost 🫠."

It is a small moment, but exactly the sort of detail that captures the rhythm of life on board: practical, slightly ridiculous, and very human.
entries.summary: Sophie captured Cameron making sure another pair of sunglasses stayed safe during the evening at Lipari.

entries.body: Cam captured a beautiful sunrise on the passage to Menorca, with SETE in tow. The sea was calm and glassy, and the boat's wake cuts through the foreground as the orange sun lifts over a pale horizon.
